page: UpCloud PREMIUM-1xCPU-2GB is a budget-tier virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features a single shared vCPU from an AMD EPYC 9575F processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server is equipped with 2.0 GB of system memory and includes 25 GB of local SSD storage, alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address. The CPU contains a 16 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, vector neural network instructions (AVX512_VNNI), and SHA extensions for cryptographic acceleration.

Benchmark results indicate highly polarized performance characteristics. The single-core processing capabilities are exceptionally strong, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all ranking in the top tier (top 10%). However, because the instance is limited to a single shared core, multi-core and parallel processing metrics fall into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is also constrained, with the PassMark memory score landing in the bottom 10% and read-only memory bandwidth registering as weak.

From a resource density perspective, this server offers a cost-effective entry point for lightweight, single-threaded applications that can leverage the high clock speed of the underlying AMD EPYC hardware without requiring sustained multi-core execution. It is poorly suited for memory-intensive databases, concurrent web serving, or multi-threaded compilation. Appropriate workloads include basic utility scripts, lightweight single-threaded automation tasks, simple static web hosting, and low-concurrency development or testing environments.
